authority: CEO R329 §Gate 5/6 — constrained new-hunt under all cemetery constraints

constraints_inherited.P-14_rule: No yield-matching candidates with SNR < 2 in CSF flow estimation
constraints_inherited.P-17_rule: No cellular surfaces in CSF without verified cell viability >30 days (endothelial cells die)
constraints_inherited.P-19_rule: No distributed-channel drainage without conductance-matched 3D verification (1D Poiseuille reverses conclusion)
constraints_inherited.P-05_rule: No flow-gated drug release in CSF without patient-population analysis (79% pass, 21% fail on low CSF flow)
constraints_inherited.P-06_rule: No membrane-based passive drainage with r⁴ scaling below required conductance
constraints_inherited.P-08_rule: No CSF kinetic energy harvesting (0.62 nW measured, insufficient for any function)
constraints_inherited.P-03_rule: No residual conductance floor without testing in obstruction/low-pressure regime (floor too small = no effect)
constraints_inherited.P-18_rule: No NO-based anti-biofilm with <7-day half-life donor (DETA-NONOate fails at 4.7 days)

search_space: Existing candidate reservoir (R268-R271 SC-A through SC-J, NC-A through NC-F) minus already promoted/killed. Plus constrained domain search in shunt failure mechanisms NOT yet covered.

SC-B.name: UWB Real-Time Intracranial Position Mapper
SC-B.mechanism: UWB microsensors at catheter tip + wearable external reader for 3D position tracking
SC-B.buyer_problem: Catheter migration/kinking causes 5-10% of shunt failures. Current detection requires CT/MRI (radiation, expensive, delayed).
SC-B.physics_risk: MEDIUM — UWB through skull is unproven. But unlike P-08 (CSF energy, measured 0.62nW), UWB through skull has published demonstrations (Apple AirTag, medical UWB imaging). Physics is plausible.
SC-B.first_evidence_action: Model UWB signal attenuation through scalp+skull+dura at 6.5 GHz. Compare to detector sensitivity threshold.
SC-B.economic_mechanism: Real-time migration detection → early intervention → avoids emergency revision surgery ($35-50K each)
SC-B.verdict: PROMOTE — admission gate passed. No fatal blocker. Physics risk is testable computationally.

SC-E.name: Pressure-Gradient Autonomous Catheter Navigation
SC-E.mechanism: Multi-segment shape-memory polymer catheter with distributed pressure sensors + autonomous navigation toward optimal drainage position
SC-E.buyer_problem: Suboptimal catheter placement causes 3-5% of shunt failures. Repositioning requires surgery.

cemetery_check.P-19: BLOCK — uses distributed pressure sensors. But this is distributed SENSING, not distributed DRAINAGE. P-19 rule applies to distributed hydraulic channels, not distributed sensing. PASS.

SC-E.admission: PASS — P-19 rule is about distributed drainage channels, not distributed sensing
SC-E.physics_risk: MEDIUM — shape-memory polymer actuation in CSF is unproven. But unlike P-17 (cells die in CSF), SMP is a material, not a living system. No fundamental biology constraint.
SC-E.first_evidence_action: Model SMP actuation force vs CSF resistance. Compare to published SMP actuation data.
SC-E.economic_mechanism: Autonomous repositioning → eliminates revision surgery for malposition
SC-E.verdict: PROMOTE — admission gate passed. No fatal blocker.

NC-E.name: Chronotherapeutic Reservoir with Drainage-Synchronized Release
NC-E.mechanism: Drug reservoir that releases medication synchronized with CSF drainage pulses (circadian pattern)
NC-E.buyer_problem: CSF drug delivery is inefficient because continuous release doesn't match physiological CSF flow patterns

cemetery_check.P-05: BLOCK — P-05 was flow-gated drug release. NC-E is drainage-SYNCHRONIZED release. Is this the same? P-05's failure was patient-population dependence (21% low-flow patients fail). NC-E synchronizes to drainage timing, not to flow rate. Different mechanism. But the ghost of P-05 is strong — any CSF-flow-coupled drug release carries the same risk. MARK AS CONDITIONAL.
cemetery_check.admission: CONDITIONAL — must verify that synchronization to drainage TIMING (not flow RATE) avoids P-05's patient-population failure
cemetery_check.verdict: CONDITIONAL — not promoted yet. Need to demonstrate mechanism is genuinely different from P-05.

NC-F.name: Fail-Operational Single-Lumen Shunt with Passive Pressure Regulation
NC-F.mechanism: Single-lumen shunt with passive pressure-regulating valve that maintains drainage across a wide ICP range without electronics
NC-F.buyer_problem: Existing shunts are single-setting. Patient needs change (posture, sleep, exercise). Fixed setting causes over/under-drainage.
NC-F.admission: PASS — no cemetery rule violated. Single-lumen (avoids P-19). Passive (no electronics). Pressure-regulating (not yield-matching).
NC-F.physics_risk: LOW — passive pressure regulation is established physics (spring-loaded valves exist). Novelty is in the wide-range passive regulation.
NC-F.first_evidence_action: Model passive valve response curve across 5-40 mmHg ICP range. Compare to existing fixed valves.
NC-F.economic_mechanism: Eliminates programmable valve adjustments → reduces clinic visits → lower cost of care
NC-F.verdict: PROMOTE — admission gate passed. Low physics risk. Clear buyer problem.

NC-E.decision: NOT PROMOTED — too similar to P-05 (cemetery). Conditional admission requires demonstrating mechanism is genuinely different from flow-gated release.
